hints: Recall which functional groups react with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNPH) to form an orange precipitate: aldehydes and ketones.
Remember that Tollens reagent is a mild oxidising agent that specifically oxidises aldehydes (forming a silver mirror) but does not react with ketones.
Look for a molecule that contains a ketone carbonyl group but no aldehyde group.
walkthrough:
**Recall the specificity of 2,4-DNPH reagent**

2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine (Bradys reagent) undergoes condensation with both aldehydes and ketones $(>\text{C}=\text{O})$ to produce an orange or yellow crystalline precipitate.

**Recall the specificity of Tollens reagent**

Tollens reagent $([\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+)$ oxidises aldehydes $(-\text{CHO})$ to carboxylate ions with deposition of metallic silver (silver mirror). It does not oxidise ketones or carboxylic acids.

**Analyze each option**

In compound A $(\text{CH}_3\text{COCO}_2\text{H})$, there is a ketone group $(\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-)$ and a carboxylic acid group $(-\text{CO}_2\text{H})$. The ketone reacts with 2,4-DNPH, but neither group reacts with Tollens reagent.
In compound B $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CHO})$, the aldehyde group reacts with Tollens reagent.
In compound C $(\text{CH}_3\text{COCHO})$, the aldehyde group also reacts with Tollens reagent.
In compound D $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3)$, propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol and lacks a carbonyl group, so it reacts with neither reagent.

options.A: Correct. 2-Oxopropanoic acid (CH3COCO2H) contains a ketone group that reacts with 2,4-DNPH, and a carboxylic acid group that does not react with Tollens reagent.
options.B: Incorrect. CH3CH(OH)CHO contains an aldehyde group (-CHO) which reduces Tollens reagent to form a silver mirror.
options.C: Incorrect. CH3COCHO contains both a ketone and an aldehyde group; the aldehyde group readily reacts with Tollens reagent.
options.D: Incorrect. Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol lacking a carbonyl group (C=O), so it does not react with 2,4-DNPH.
